morning.insight:
💡 형, 화요일 아침입니다. 간밤 미국 증시가 엔비디아 CEO 복귀 호재로 크게 반등하며 '검은 월요일'의 무게를 덜었습니다.

**심리는 개선, 수급은 미지수.** 나스닥 +6.47%, 엔비디아 +31%라는 강한 되돌림은 분명 반가운 소식이지만, 어제 국내에서 외국인이 7거래일 연속 순매도했고 원/달러가 1,348원대로 올라온 점은 여전히 부담입니다. 반등 출발은 예상되나, 되돌림의 지속성은 외국인 수급 회복과 반도체 업종 차별화에 달려 있습니다.

**황 복귀는 '해법'이지 '구조 해소'는 아닙니다.** 젠슨 황 복귀로 AI 트레이드 신뢰가 회복됐지만, AI 투자 수익성·부채 부담·정치적 규제 리스크는 그대로입니다. 단기 급등에 추격 매수하기보다 밸류체인 내 옥석 가리기가 필요한 국면입니다.

**오늘 손에 잡을 3건.** ① T-P19 월 경영수지(0%인데 내일 11/25 보고) — 오늘 착수해야 합니다. ② Z-P11 우수성공실패사례(종료 11/26) — 내일 심사결과 발표·자료 수정요청 준비. ③ T-P5 제니엘플러스(11/26 결과보고·11/28 품의) — 이번 주 중간 점검이 필요합니다.

폭락 다음 날의 반등은 늘 반갑지만, 형이 실제로 통제할 수 있는 건 시장이 아니라 손에 쥔 이 세 가지 일입니다. 경영수지·사례 심사·제니엘플러스, 이 셋부터 정리해 봅니다.

articles.headline: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.body: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president, capping one of the most startling corporate comebacks after a fast-moving scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The board said the decision came after input from senior U.S. government officials.

articles.headline: Nasdaq Jumps, Nvidia Surges After Huang Returns as CEO
articles.body: The Nasdaq jumped and Nvidia surged after Jensen Huang returned as CEO, helping markets recover from last week's AI-driven selloff in the strongest rally since April 2025.

articles.headline: A Timeline of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Spy Downfall and Resurrection
articles.body: The scandal put the world's most consequential AI CEO in the hot seat and cost him his job — until the U.S. government intervened. The timeline traces Huang's downfall and rapid resurrection at Nvidia.

articles.headline: The Campaign to Bring Back Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.body: In open letters, phone calls and group chats, Huang's allies made the case that his ouster was hasty — even as legal scrutiny intensified around his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

articles.headline: Top Republican Senator Says Lutnick Ignored His China Chip Warnings
articles.body: A top Republican senator said Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick ignored his warnings about China chip risks, an exclusive report amid heightened scrutiny of U.S. semiconductor policy.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO
articles.body: In his first public remarks since resigning, Huang said an outpouring of support from friends and colleagues had been overwhelming, signaling his willingness to return to the corner office.

articles.headline: Nvidia Rehires Huang in Stunning Reversal After Trump Push
articles.body: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as head of the world's largest chipmaker in one of the most startling corporate comebacks, sending the stock on its biggest rally in decades. Huang reclaims the president and CEO titles less than two weeks after leaving under a cloud of scandal.

articles.headline: Stocks Jump Most Since April 2025 as Huang Is Back: Markets Wrap
articles.body: Global stocks jumped the most since April 2025 as Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia, fueling a broad risk-on rally after last week's worst weekly selloff since the spring of 2025.

articles.headline: Trump Enlisted Vance in Campaign to Rescue Nvidia's Jensen Huang
articles.body: President Trump enlisted JD Vance in a campaign to rescue Nvidia's Jensen Huang, praising the board's decision to reinstate him as CEO and casting the move as crucial to the AI race with China.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang Will Testify Publicly Before Senators Next Week
articles.body: Jensen Huang will testify publicly before U.S. senators next week, keeping the scrutiny of Nvidia and its returned CEO in the spotlight amid bipartisan demands for answers.

articles.headline: Yardeni Cuts S&P 500 Target Again, Says Bear Market Is Unlikely
articles.body: Ed Yardeni cut his S&P 500 target again but said a bear market is unlikely, arguing that the recent AI-driven selloff was an overreaction to a concentrated leadership shakeup.

articles.headline: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO: Live Updates

articles.body: Trump's intervention to reinstate the Nvidia boss sets a dangerous precedent, and risks emboldening other tech barons to believe they can act with impunity, argues the FT's editorial board.
